citation.quote: This Agreement renews automatically for further 12-month periods unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 30 days before the end of the current term.
The Customer shall pay monthly fees of INR 3,00,000, invoiced on the 1st of each month starting 1 February 2026.

findings.claim: Nimbus can unilaterally increase fees by 30 days email notice, creating unpredictable cost escalation with no cap or negotiation requirement

debate.rationale: Clause 3.2 explicitly states 'The Provider may revise the fees at any time on 30 days notice by email.' This confirms Nimbus can unilaterally increase fees with only 30 days notice. The claim is accurate - there is no cap on fee increases and no negotiation requirement in the clause.

citations.quote: The Provider may revise the fees at any time on 30 days notice by email.

Acme must either accept the increase or exercise termination rights (but only if within the 30-day non-renewal window). 4. debate.argument: THOR's clarification reveals that the Nimbus cap (10% of monthly fee) is likely a monthly aggregate cap, not per-incident. The phrase 'For each 0.5% (or part)...' with the cap at the end of the clause structure suggests credits accumulate but are capped at 10% total per month. For each 0.5% (or part) by which availability falls below 99.5%, the Customer is entitled to a service credit of 5% of the monthly fee, capped at 10% of the monthly fee.
The Provider's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid by the Customer in the 3 months preceding the claim.

findings.claim: Nimbus can suspend services after just 45 days non-payment without prior notice, potentially causing immediate catastrophic breach of Acme's BigRetail commitments with no opportunity to cure

debate.rationale: Clause 4.3 states 'If any amount remains unpaid for more than 45 days the Provider may suspend the Services without further notice.' This confirms Nimbus can suspend services after 45 days non-payment with no prior notice required. The claim accurately describes this hidden liability.

citations.quote: If any amount remains unpaid for more than 45 days the Provider may suspend the Services without further notice.

findings.attack_path: 1. Acme faces temporary cash flow issue (e.g., BigRetail delays payment). 2. Acme's payment to Nimbus is 15+ days late. 3. Nimbus immediately suspends services 'without further notice' upon day 46. 4. BigRetail platform goes down. 5. BigRetail invokes immediate termination and damages under CSA-2026-004 clause 4.3. 6. citations.quote: The Landlord may terminate this lease by giving the Tenant 30 days written notice.
The Tenant may terminate this lease only by giving the Landlord 6 months written notice and paying rent for the notice period in advance.

verifications.rationale: Clause 5.1 explicitly states 'The Landlord may terminate this lease by giving the Tenant 30 days written notice.' Clause 5.2 states 'The Tenant may terminate this lease only by giving the Landlord 6 months written notice and paying rent for the notice period in advance.' The claim accurately reflects the asymmetric termination rights - 30 days vs 6 months (180 days) plus advance rent payment requi…

citations.quote: The Tenant shall indemnify the Landlord against all losses, claims and expenses arising from the use of the Premises, without limit.

verifications.rationale: Clause 6.1 states 'The Tenant shall indemnify the Landlord against all losses, claims and expenses arising from the use of the Premises, without limit.' The claim is accurate - there is no carve-out for Landlord's own negligence or misconduct. The word 'use of the Premises' suggests this covers third-party claims arising from tenant activities, but the clause is broad and unlimited as claimed.
